synopsis: Fractional factorial design reduces experimental run count by testing only a chosen fraction of combinations, but deliberately introduces aliasing that makes some higher-order effects indistinguishable [f6800, f14102]. A finding of no main effect for fog therefore cannot rule out a localized, non-linear failure involving a particular combination of fog density, glare and sensor contamination [f6809, f14108]. The glossary also cautions that DOE cannot find a narrow failure region hidden between design points, limiting what planners can infer from apparently reassuring results [f14108].

relations.note: Both describe reduced run counts and aliasing of higher-order effects.
Both warn that no fog main effect does not exclude a localized combination-specific failure.
Aliasing higher-order effects helps explain why absent main effects cannot exclude combination-specific failures.
